_meta.comment: Sibling groups for KaiSip's CIA packs (plan CIA_BANK_PLAN.md section 3 decision 4 and section 11, expert decisions of 27 Nov 2026): items in one group teach the same or a neighbouring lesson, so the app shows at most one per mock, held-back form or practice session. Groups may span parts; the app applies each group within each pack (the Challenge pack included, through its source ids). Built from each live item's _provenance and the coverage maps' sibling lists, judged by lesson (nearest-item and shared-option mentions that do not share a keyed lesson are left out). Hand-maintained: log a new sibling here and in the item's _provenance.

groups.lesson: Assurance answers a board request for confidence against criteria
Advisory work gives advice, never a conclusion on effectiveness
Training is advisory; management designs and owns the controls
Advisory output (a map, facilitated ratings) gives no assurance until evaluated
Assurance may follow advisory work once objectivity is confirmed
Due diligence work and what may follow it
Due diligence and forensic support are advisory services
A contract audit: the contract sets the criteria and the access
Scope limitations: whatever stops planned work, raised with management then the board
A cut or shortfall in internal audit's resources or approved scope goes promptly to the board
Management limiting internal audit's work or independence goes to the board
Impairments to independence and the yearly confirmation to the board
A role that could impair independence goes to the board and senior management
The mandate's parts: authority, role and responsibilities
The board creates internal audit's authority; senior management supports it
Who acts as the board for internal audit
The board appoints the chief audit executive and sets the role
What the charter must hold, including legal requirements
Another set of requirements sits beside the Standards, never in their place
The board decides charter content; senior management's views are input
Tasks internal audit must not own under the 2026 risk management statement
Choosing risk responses stays with management
Running a control is first-line work internal audit would then assess
A significant risk met in advisory work is still reported as a finding
Three Lines: management's own operations and monitoring are first line
Outside providers are bound and supervised like staff
Laws that require disclosure of a violation are followed
Where to send an ethics or fraud concern when policy is silent
When a result changes: verified evidence, not disagreement
A finding is rated at its true significance, never traded or inflated
An overdue action goes to the chief audit executive, not into the rating
Gifts and favors that may impair objectivity are refused
Self-review bias when judging one's own earlier work
Due care weighs the organization's current strategy, not only targets
Releasing engagement records follows the function's methodology
Research tests criteria and models against several sources
Work an auditor can become competent for, with fitting supervision
Auditors train for the specific skill or tool before the work
Skepticism seeks restore-test evidence that recovery works
Management may choose its own remedy; the agreed action is followed up
Culture and behavioral risk are read from behavior, not rules or messages
Conduct is measured against the organization's own expectations, not only rules
Reporting conduct that departs from the organization's ethical expectations
What compliance covers: contracts, policies and new activities' rules
What makes a finding: criteria in force, a gap, a significant risk
An assurance conclusion judges effectiveness and says so when criteria are met
Locating the failed step among the five risk management elements
Risk appetite and tolerance: when accepted risk must be raised
A control is any action that manages a risk
A control is weak in design when transactions can pass outside it
Criteria must be adequate; if not, settle them with the board or senior management
A design gap seen in a walk-through comes before operating tests
Stalled action and accepted risk: the chief audit executive's route
What informs the plan's risk assessment, management's register included
Whether the plan includes a topic is decided on risk
Coordinating with other assurance providers, and when it fails
Fraud exposure ranks by significance and by lost independent checks
Fraud covers information and non-cash figures, not only assets taken
Reporting a fraud concern: the route and the content
Investigators' cases and complaint trends as planning input
An authority level prevents fraud only if enforced on the whole job
Tone at the top shows in what leaders do and reward
Integrity of fraud investigations and their evidence
A risk or gap shared across units is judged by its reach
Separating ordering, receiving and paying, or adding an independent check
An earlier assessment is an input to update, not the current evidence
Relevance is judged against the question, apart from reliability
Topical Requirement applicability: assurance on the topic conforms, each requirement assessed, exclusions reasoned
The Cybersecurity requirement, not a framework, sets what assurance covers
Third-party risk stays the organization's: assess management's oversight of vendors
The Third-Party requirement's reach: subcontractors in, intragroup providers out
What the work program and project plan must contain
The tested population must be able to show the exception for the whole period
Agile cycles still need each work program change approved
Recovery objectives: recovery point against recovery time and tolerable downtime
Classifying balance sheet items by timing, intent and nature
A tool's or file's output is relied on only once its logic and data are checked
Reliability of the source decides the method: system record or observation
Observation where no record exists, a reliable record where one does
A weak source system is not repaired by who extracts or reruns the data
Pick the analysis that answers the objective
Fit the analysis to the data's structure
Make data comparable before testing or combining it
The condition comes from how the process ran, not from a map
Independent payroll drivers and which differences to follow up
One price-override condition: ranked by significance, then fixed at its cause
A timing change is communicated; a work program change needs approval
What reaches management at the start of an engagement
The chief audit executive decides the form and recipients of final communications
Methodologies the chief audit executive must set, update after a change and train on
Significant plan changes and displaced assurance go to the board
Advice drawn from the plan's reserve is weighed and reported, not approved
The budget funds the plan and the strategy, and the board approves it
Relying on another provider: a documented basis, disclosed in conclusions
Ongoing monitoring and the periodic self-assessment: mirror duties
What the quality results report to the board holds
Who may assess quality: qualified and independent assessors
Nonconformance: one engagement's own report against a function-wide gap
Correcting an issued report: significant errors only, for every recipient
A low risk rating management vouches for, re-weighed by the chief audit executive
